title: Compatibility of lifted maps
statement: Let $X$ be Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $I,K$ be quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme], let $M$ be a coherent $I$-adic system [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and $H$ a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent]. Assume for each $q\ge1$ that completion on $V(K^q)$ with respect to $I\mathcal O_{V(K^q)}$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is an equivalence, for every Noetherian instance. Given $\alpha:M\to\widehat H_I$, a natural double-system isomorphism $\theta_{e,n}:(H/K^{e+1}H)/I^{n+1}\cong(H/I^{n+1}H)/K^{e+1}$, a coherent $K$-adic system $N$, and a doubly natural isomorphism $\sigma_{e,n}:N_e/I^{n+1}N_e\cong M_n/K^{e+1}M_n$, there exists $\delta:N\to\widehat H_K$ such that for all $e,n\ge0$, $\sigma_{e,n}$ followed by $\alpha_n$ modulo $K^{e+1}$ equals $\delta_e$ modulo $I^{n+1}$ followed by $\theta_{e,n}$. The map $\delta$ is constructed by lifting, rather than supplied independently.

proof.text: For coherent modules supported on a closed subscheme j, transport them through the coherent closed-pushforward equivalence. Closed pushforward is fully faithful, and the natural completion comparison identifies ambient I-completion with pushforward of completion on the subscheme. The assumed equivalence there gives a bijection on ambient completed Hom sets. Transport the bijection along the endpoint isomorphisms. This is supported_completion_bijective. Endpoint transport reuses the proved private map_bijective_of_isos in GrothendieckExistenceSupportedHom via import all; no proper-completion result or additional geometric hypothesis is used.

For modules killed by possibly different positive K-powers, raise the two annihilating powers to their maximum using formalModuleQuotient_factor. Use the proved power_subobject and product_iso helpers of IdealPowerProductRestrictionZero to identify the recursively defined ideal powers with (K^q).toModules, hence with the kernel ideal of V(K^q). Apply the supported Hom bijection on that common thickening. This is torsion_completion_bijective.

Set Q = completion_K(H). Form the morphism of double systems tau = sigma.hom followed by the flipped K-completion of alpha followed by theta.inv. Each term N_e and Q_e is coherent and annihilated by K^(e+1), by the defining coherent-adic conditions. Surjectivity of the supported Hom bijection lifts tau_e to d_e with completion_I(d_e) = tau_e. Injectivity specifies the lift uniquely.

For an adjacent K-transition, complete the two composites involving the d_e. The functor composition law and the lifting equations reduce their equality to naturality of tau. The supported Hom bijection for N_(e+1) and Q_e is injective, hence the original composites agree. NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles d into delta. Evaluate its lifting equation at n and compose with theta.hom; theta.inv_hom_id gives the comparison square.

lean.statement:
theorem grothendieckDevissage_secondAdicSystem_lift_compatibility
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (M : CoherentFormalModule X I)
    (hthick : ∀ (e : ℕ), 1 ≤ e →
      ∀ (hZ : IsNoetherian (K ^ e).subscheme),
        Functor.IsEquivalence
          (@completion ((K ^ e).subscheme) hZ (I.comap (K ^ e).subschemeι)))
    (H : CoherentModules X) (α : M ⟶ (completion X I).obj H)
    (θ : formalCompletionSystem K H.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor I ≅
      (formalCompletionSystem I H.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor K).flip)
    {N : CoherentFormalModule X K}
    (σ : N.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor I ≅
      (M.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor K).flip) :
    ∃ (δ : N ⟶ (completion X K).obj H), ∀ e n : ℕ,
      (σ.hom.app (op e)).app (op n) ≫
          formalModuleQuotientMap K (α.hom.app (op n)) (Nat.le_refl (e + 1)) =
        formalModuleQuotientMap I (δ.hom.app (op e)) (Nat.le_refl (n + 1)) ≫
          (θ.hom.app (op e)).app (op n)
